item.title: Lord of the Rings-inspired Utah estate gets $5 million price cut, now asks $38 million
item.description: A 30-acre estate in Provo, Utah, inspired byThe Lord of the Rings, is now listed for $38 million after a $5 million price cut. The 32-room property includes a nearly 23,000-square-foot main house, a guesthouse over a private pond, waterfalls, pools, sports facilities and private trails. The current owners bought it in 2017 and later added the pond and guesthouse.

Charlie Kirk Shooting: Utah man sues Candace Owens; alleges podcast defamation
item.description: A Utah man has sued Candace Owens, alleging she falsely linked him to Charlie Kirk’s 2026 shooting at Utah Valley University. Robert Hild Jr. claims Owens used social media photos and podcast episodes to suggest he had ties to the suspect and foreign groups. He says the allegations damaged his reputation, exposed his family’s personal information and led to threats, vandalism and safety concerns.

item.title: In the early 1970s, David Wolkowsky began stewarding a remote island near Key West and...
item.description: Ballast Key, a stunning private island located near Key West, is now officially a part of the Key West National Wildlife Refuge. This crucial ownership shift aims to safeguard the island from potential developments. Once the retreat of prominent figures like David Wolkowsky, it is now vital for the biodiversity it supports, ensuring that diverse wildlife can thrive as conservation efforts continue for its preservation.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Forty-five North Carolina property owners sued over roads planned through their neighborhoods
item.description: The Hilton Bluffs project in North Carolina is facing legal challenges regarding access road routes. Local residents have filed a lawsuit against Copper Builders, objecting to pathways that intrude on private land. Even after revised plans were submitted, local authorities deemed them unsafe, leading to continued construction delays. As both sides gear up for legal hearings, the situation underscores the intense demand for housing in the area.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: US to lend 40m barrel oil from strategic reserve as Ukraine war strains supply
item.description: The United States has proposed a loan of 40 million barrels of oil from its Strategic Petroleum Reserve to energy companies. This initiative is designed to counteract rising oil prices, which have been significantly impacted by the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. As Indian refiners brace for a decline in Russian oil supplies, competition with China is pushing them toward pricier oil options.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: Reno’s 1868 house was sold for $1, but there was one catch
item.description: The Benham-Belz House, the oldest surviving house in Reno, was relocated to preserve its legacy. Originally built in 1868, the house has a rich history that reflects Reno's development. It was sold for $1 under the condition that it be moved and restored. The relocation occurred in July 2025, marking the end of its 150-year presence on the original site.

item.title: Farmland Protected From Development: Biddle grants conservation easement; 170 acres stay in agriculture
item.description: Dairy farmer Jeff Biddle has placed his Bear Meadows Farm under a permanent conservation easement for protection. The decision came after Biddle declined two offers from potential buyers interested in the property. The conservation easement ensures that the farm's agricultural landscape will remain intact without development. Biddle's family has farmed the land since 1959, emphasizing the farm's long-standing history.

item.title: In 1964, an Arizona couple began building a carport with discarded bottles; years later...
item.description: A couple in Tucson, Arizona, transformed glass bottles into a 2,700-square-foot home over several decades. They used discarded bottles collected from local sources to construct the unique property and create a natural cooling effect. After completion, the house was maintained by an artist who updated essential systems while preserving original features. The property has now been listed for sale, attracting interest from folk art enthusiasts.

item.title: How Russia's ballistic missiles, jet-powered drones have kept Ukraine under pressure
item.description: Reports indicate that Russia is intensifying its attacks on Ukraine, targeting key cities with ballistic missiles and drones. As Ukraine grapples with a lack of US-made Patriot missiles, the capability of its air defenses is being severely tested. Ukrainian officials claim that these strikes are a strategic move by Russia to weaken their defense.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: A Utah man who spent 41 years in jail in a 1985 murder case has been ordered released on bail after...
item.description: After spending 41 years on death row for the murder of Eva Olesen, Douglas Stewart Carter is finally released on bail following new DNA evidence proving his innocence. The Utah Supreme Court acknowledged serious police misconduct in the case. Although some family members of the victim have raised concerns regarding his bail, a retrial is set for 2027, with defense lawyers hopeful to have all charges dismissed.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Taylor Swift’s former Beverly Hills estate where she wrote ‘1989’ listed for $7.995M after renovations
item.description: Taylor Swift’s former Beverly Hills estate, where she wrote her hit album 1989, is back on the market for $7.995 million. The 1.5-acre Pillsbury Estate features a main residence, guest house, four bedrooms, five bathrooms, mature oak trees, a pickleball court and an eight-car motor court following extensive renovations by its current owners.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: 575+ Nevada volunteers removed 120,125 pounds of waste across 26 Truckee River sites in one day
item.description: On September 26, over 575 passionate volunteers dedicated their time to a significant cleanup effort in Nevada's Truckee River watershed. Their hard work resulted in the removal of an astounding 120,125 pounds of waste, which included both litter and invasive weeds. This collaborative initiative also focused on planting vegetation and enhancing storm drains, all aimed at safeguarding the local ecosystem.
